memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Set up the tabernacle according to the plan shown you on the mountain." - Exodus 26:30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the detailed instructions, God gives the summary command again: build it according to the plan shown you on the mountain. Not according to Moses' judgment, not according to what seemed practical, and not according to what the surrounding nations did with their shrines. God's dwelling was to be built God's way.

Moses had seen something on that mountain that no one else had seen. His task was faithfulness to what he had been shown, even in details whose purpose he may not have fully understood. That is often the shape of obedience — doing what God has clearly said before we can see all the reasons why.

We face the same choice constantly. God has revealed how we are to live, how we are to treat others, how we are to come to Him. The temptation is always to adjust the plan slightly, to build according to what seems reasonable to us or acceptable to the culture around us. But Jesus said the wise builder is the one who hears His words and puts them into practice (Matt 7:24). Faithfulness to God's revealed pattern is not rigidity; it is trust. He sees the whole design, and we see a part.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where am I tempted to adjust God's clear instructions to suit my own judgment?
Can I obey God in something whose full purpose I do not yet understand?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see the whole design while I see only a part. Give me the trust to follow Your revealed way faithfully, even when I do not fully understand it. Amen.
